sentences.text: The Detailed Accident Report (hereinafter referred to as DAR), was filed in this case on 09.01.2020, with reference to FIR No. 339/19, U/s 279/338 IPC, PS Shalimar Bagh, Delhi, in respect of grievous hurt, sustained by the injured Vipin Kumar Gupta, in a road traffic accident, on 22.07.2019, at about 7.40 am, at Satyawati Flyover, Ashok Vihar, Delhi.

The Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal, vide order dated 09.01.2020, treated the DAR, as claim petition MACT No. 18/20 Page 4 of24 Vipin Kumar Gupta vs Dinesh Singh and Anr. Page 5 of24 U/s 166(4) of the M.V. Act.

sentences.text: Subsequently, chargesheet was filed by the IO, against Dinesh Singh S/o Sh. Rajmal Singh, driver of the offending vehicle (hereinafter referred as to as the driver of the offending vehicle/respondent no.1/R1), for the alleged commission of offence U/s 279/338 IPC and U/s 56/192 and U/s 66(1)/192A, 146/196 of M.V. Act, because, as per the opinion on the MLC of the petitioner, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the case accident and R1 failed to produce Registration Certificate, fitness, permit and insurance policy.

2. The brief facts of the case, as discernible from the DAR and documents of the petitioner namely Vipin Kumar Gupta (hereinafter referred as petitioner/claimant/ injured), are that on 22.07.2019,
the petitioner was going to drop three children in a school from Tri Nagar to Gujrawala Town, Delhi in his E-rickshaw bearing registration No. DL-9T-CE-1144 (hereinafter referred to as victim's vehicle), and when he reached at Satyawati Flyover, Ashok Vihar, Delhi, the victim's vehicle was hit,
by one Tempo traveller bearing registration no. DL-1VC-1444 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle), which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner, by its driver/R1 Dinesh Singh S/o Sh. Rajmal Singh and as a result of the said impact, the victim's vehicle turned turtle and the petitioner alongwith the three children fell down on the road and sustained injuries.

It was further averred that after the accident, R1 boarded the petitioner in an auto MACT No. 18/20 Page 5 of24 Vipin Kumar Gupta vs Dinesh Singh and Anr. Page 6 of24 rickshaw for taking him to hospital but on the way to hospital, the petitioner met his brother who got him admitted in the Balaji Action Hospital, Paschim Vihar, Delhi (hereinafter referred to as Balaji Hospital), where he was medically examined, vide MLC No. 8423/2019, as per which, he has sustained grievous injuries in the case accident.
3. As per DAR, at the time of accident, the offending vehicle was driven by R1, the same was registered in the name of Prince Gulati S/o Late Sh. Ashok Kumar Gulati, but, the same was un-insured.
4. R1 and R2 failed to contest the claim petition/DAR, R1 and R2 had appeared only once at the time of filing of DAR and thereafter stopped appearing and thus, their defence was struck off on 22.12.2022 and thereafter, they were proceeded Ex-parte, vide order dated 19.01.2024.

His deposition qua the accident in question and injuries sustained by him, in the case accident, is reiteration of the contents of the DAR/claim petition.

10. On appreciation of evidence, as adduced by the parties, in support of their respective versions,
the issue-wise findings of this Tribunal are reproduced herein below:
Whether on 22.07.2019 at about 07.40 am, at Satyawati Flyover, Ashok Vihar, Delhi,
one Tempo Travel bearing registration no. DL-1VC-1444 which was being driven rashly and negligent by R1/Dinesh Singh, had hit the E-rickshaw bearing registration no. DL-9TCE-1144 and caused injuries to Vipin Kumar Gupta?
OPP 11.
The onus of proving this issue, on preponderance of probabilities was upon the petitioner/claimant.
For deciding the present issue, the testimony of PW1 Vipin Kumar Gupta, is relevant, being an eyewitness as well as the injured.

PW1 deposed that on 22.07.2019, he was going to drop three children in a school from Tri Nagar to Gujrawala Town, Delhi in his E-rickshaw bearing registration No. DL-9T-CE-1144 and when he reached at Satyawati Flyover, Ashok Vihar,
Delhi, the victim's vehicle was hit, by one Tempo traveller bearing registration no. DL-1VC-1444,
which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner, by its driver/R1 Dinesh Singh S/o Sh.
Rajmal Singh and as a result of the said impact, the victim's vehicle turned turtle and he alongwith the three MACT No. 18/20 Page 9 of24 Vipin Kumar Gupta vs Dinesh Singh and Anr. Page 10 of24 children fell down on the road and sustained injuries.

In view of the above said discussion, criminal case record including charge sheet and testimony of PW1 Vipin Kumar Gupta, it has been proved by preponderance of probabilities that the case accident had been caused by R1, who was driving the offending vehicle, bearing no. DL-1VC-1444, in a rash and negligent manner, at the above said date, time and place and had hit the petitioner, due to which, the petitioner had sustained injuries.
Issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents accordingly.
Whether petitioner is entitled to compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?OPP 15.
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry, into the claim to make an award, determining the amount of compensation, which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind, that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly.
MEDICAL EXPENSES 16.

To prove the amount spent by the petitioner, on his treatment, the petitioner got himself examined as PW1, by MACT No. 18/20 Page 11 of24 Vipin Kumar Gupta vs Dinesh Singh and Anr.
Page 12 of24 way of evidence affidavit Ex.PW1/A, wherein he deposed that he has spent a sum of Rs.
2,50,000/-, on his treatment and medical bills.

sentences.text: In his evidence, the petitioner/PW1 has placed reliance on his treatment record and medical bills as Mark-X.
PW1 further deposed that he had taken mediclaim policy from National Insurance Co. Ltd. and the said company has reimbursed part amount and the remaining amount was paid by him.
However, petitioner has failed to place on record any documentary proof as to amount for non reimbursement of the medical bills from the hospital.

Moreover, the medical bills have been verified by the IO from the concerned hospital but the petitioner has failed to place on record any documentary proof which would reflect that the certain amount was reimbursed to him and certain other amount has not been reimbursed to him.
Thus, this Tribunal deems it appropriate, to award NIL compensation to the petitioner, under the head of medical expenses.
SPECIAL DIET AND CONVEYANCE 17.
The petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs. 50,000/- , on account of expenditure, incurred by him on special diet and conveyance, as a result of the injuries sustained in the case accident.

The petitioner has, however, failed to place on record, prescription of any doctor or medical practitioner or dietitian, containing details of special diet, such as, nutritional supplements, prescribed to him,
for MACT No. 18/20 Page 12 of24 Vipin Kumar Gupta vs Dinesh Singh and Anr. Page 13 of24 speedy recovery of the injuries, sustained by him, in the case accident.

Accordingly, the entitlement of the petitioner, to compensation if any, towards special diet and conveyance charges, has to be determined, in accordance with the nature of injuries, sustained by the petitioner/victim, in the case accident.

In this context, a perusal of MLC No. 8423/19, as well as medical treatment record and medical bills Mark-X, of the petitioner Vipin Kumar Gupta, reveals that after examination of the petitioner,
the doctor has given the opinion, that he has sustained grievous injuries, in the case accident.
As per the said MLC, the petitioner has suffered compound fracture of both bone right forearm.

Perusal of medical treatment record of petitioner further reveals that he remained admitted in Balaji Action Hospital from 22.07.2019 to 25.07.2019 and he again admitted in the said hospital from 27.07.2019 to 01.08.2019 for undergoing surgery of the aforesaid injuries.

Therefore, keeping in view the grievous nature of injuries, sustained by the petitioner, the treatment cum recuperation period, in case of the petitioner is determined to be about 06 months and during this period, the petitioner must have incurred MACT No. 18/20 Page 13 of24 Vipin Kumar Gupta vs Dinesh Singh and Anr.
Page 14 of24 expenses, on special diet, required for his speedy recovery, as well as on travel to various hospitals and clinics, from his residence and vice versa.

Accordingly, a lump sum amount of Rs.40,000/-, is granted to the petitioner, as compensation under this head, including Rs.20,000/-
each, towards special diet and conveyance respectively.
ATTENDANT CHARGES 19.
The petitioner has claimed compensation, on account of attendant charges, as a result of the injuries sustained in the case accident.

He has however, not disclosed the exact expenditure,
incurred by him, on availing services of medical attendant, during his treatment period.

20. Further, a perusal of court record reveals that the petitioner has neither placed on record, any bill, raised by any agency, from which, he has hired a medical attendant nor examined the concerned attendant, hired by him or any employee of the agency, through which he had hired the said attendant.

However, as discussed above, regarding the medical condition of the petitioner, as per which, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the case accident, as he has suffered composite fracture of both bone forearm and determination of his period of treatment cum recuperation as six months, this Tribunal is of the opinion, that due to the injuries sustained by him,
in the case accident, he must have required services of either a MACT No. 18/20 Page 14 of24 Vipin Kumar Gupta vs Dinesh Singh and Anr. Page 15 of24 paid attendant or a family member, as an attendant, for his self-care activities.

sentences.text: Thus, this Tribunal deems it appropriate, to award a lump sum amount of Rs.20,000/-, as compensation to the petitioner, under this head, towards attendant charges.
PAIN AND SUFFERING 21.

In the present case, as per MLC no. 8423/19 as well as medical treatment record, of the petitioner Vipin Kumar Gupta, he has suffered grievous injuries and it was also observed that the petitioner has suffered composite fracture of both bone forearm.
He deposed that he has suffered pain and agony, due to the injuries sustained by him in the case accident.

Further, the treatment cum recuperation period of the petitioner, has already been assessed as six months, therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion, that the petitioner must have suffered physical pain and mental agony,
during his treatment cum recuperation period.
Accordingly, a lump sum amount of Rs.40,000/-, is granted under the said head to the petitioner.

However, as per disability report, issued by Dr. BSA Hospital reveals that the petitioner has not suffered any disability due to the injuries sustained in the case accident.
Moreover, the petitioner has failed to prove on record that he used to run e-rickshaw and also engaged in catering works at the time of accident.

23. To prove his income, the petitioner has also placed reliance upon his ITR, for the assessment year 2018-2019, as per which, his annual income was shown as Rs.3,37,826/-, and after addition of deduction of income tax, his net income would come to Rs.3,36,790/.

Therefore, on the date of accident, the monthly income of the petitioner is taken as Rs.28,065.83 and since, this Tribunal has already assessed the treatment-cum- recuperation period of the petitioner as 06 months, therefore,
considering the nature of injuries, as sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the taxi service of the petitioner, must have been adversely affected, at least for a period of 6 months.

Therefore, a sum of Rs. 1,68,395/- (Rs.28,065.83 x 6 months), is awarded in favour of the petitioner, as compensation under MACT No. 18/20 Page 16 of24 Vipin Kumar Gupta vs Dinesh Singh and Anr. Page 17 of24 the head of loss of income.

LIABILITY 27.

In the case in hand, the offending vehicle is admittedly un-insured at the time of accident and it has already come on record, that at the time of accident, respondent was driving the offending vehicle and the accident has been caused, due to rash and negligent driving, of the offending vehicle by respondent.

6 14. opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
12. Both R1 and R2 failed to file any written statement, thus, they both deemed to have admitted involvement of the offending vehicle, in the case accident and rashness and negligence on the part of R1, in causing the accident.
R1 and R2 further chose not to appear in the court, so as to bring out falsity qua the present claim petition/DAR, by the cross-examination of PW1 and even failed to elicit any admission from the testimony of PW1, so as to negate the fact that the petitioner has sustained injuries, due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R1.
13.
Further, there is nothing on record which shows that driver of the offending vehicle/R1 has ever approached to any higher authority, with respect to his false implication in the present case.
The fact that the petitioner's injuries sustained in the accident stand duly corroborated by the MLC of PW1(petitioner), which clearly records that the injuries were the result of a road traffic accident.
It has to be borne in mind, that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly.
Accordingly, the entitlement of the petitioner, to compensation if any, towards special diet and conveyance charges, has to be determined, in accordance with the nature of injuries, sustained by the petitioner/victim, in the case accident.
Therefore, keeping in view the grievous nature of injuries, sustained by the petitioner, the treatment cum recuperation period, in case of the petitioner is determined to be about 06 months and during this period, the petitioner must have incurred MACT No. 18/20 Page 13 of24 Vipin Kumar Gupta vs Dinesh Singh and Anr.
Page 14 of24 expenses, on special diet, required for his speedy recovery, as well as on travel to various hospitals and clinics, from his residence and vice versa.
20. Further, a perusal of court record reveals that the petitioner has neither placed on record, any bill, raised by any agency, from which, he has hired a medical attendant nor examined the concerned attendant, hired by him or any employee of the agency, through which he had hired the said attendant.
Therefore, on the date of accident, the monthly income of the petitioner is taken as Rs.28,065.83 and since, this Tribunal has already assessed the treatment-cum- recuperation period of the petitioner as 06 months, therefore,
considering the nature of injuries, as sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the taxi service of the petitioner, must have been adversely affected, at least for a period of 6 months.
In respect of entitlement of the petitioner to interest on the awarded amount, it is noteworthy that the Hon'ble Apex Court had in the case of Municipal Corporation of Delhi vs. Association of Victims of Uphaar Tragedy, 2012 ACJ 48 (SC) had observed that the victims of Uphaar Tragedy be awarded compensation with interest @ 9% per annum.
Therefore, in the interest of justice, in the present case, this court is of the opinion that MACT No. 18/20 Page 17 of24 Vipin Kumar Gupta vs Dinesh Singh and Anr. Page 18 of24 the claimant/petitioner is entitled to interest at the prevailing bank rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of DAR/petition, that is, with effect from 09.01.2020 till realization of the compensation amount.
In the case in hand, the offending vehicle is admittedly un-insured at the time of accident and it has already come on record, that at the time of accident, respondent was driving the offending vehicle and the accident has been caused, due to rash and negligent driving, of the offending vehicle by respondent.
Even otherwise, perusal of record reveals that the chargesheet was filed by the IO,
against Dinesh Singh S/o Sh. Rajmal Singh, driver of the offending vehicle, for the alleged commission of offence U/s 279/338 IPC and U/s 56/192 and U/s 66(1)/192A, 146/196 of M.V. Act,
because R1 failed to produce registration Certificate, fitness, permit and insurance policy at the time of accident, Thus, R1 and R2, being driver and registered owner of the offending vehicle respectively, are jointly and severally liable to pay the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
